what_it_does: scans the cached event tuples for the first matching event of each user in `remaining`, returning {user: [(event_type, issue)]}

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: once found holds every user of `remaining`, no later event can add anything (each actor is added at most once, only if in remaining); breaking there stops the scan of a cache that holds up to four months of events per repo

what_it_does: pages through a repo's issue comments since cutoff and builds {user: {'pr': [numbers], 'issue': [numbers]}}

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `number not in list` scans a growing list per comment; a local set of (user, kind, number) keeps the same output lists with an O(1) probe. The lists are the cached return value and keep insertion order

what_it_does: batches GraphQL review searches for 10 users at a time, then REST-verifies candidate PRs and paginates per user

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the sanitised alias name is rebuilt by a regex sub per user twice; compute once per batch and reuse for the read

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: the guard is unreachable because range slicing yields non-empty slices; repair is deleting it, expected gain nil

what_it_does: checks a team's maintainers for comments, reviews, authored PRs and merges across repos, short-circuiting per user

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: _search_fields() returns a constant for the run; calling it per user adds one call per user. Hoist before the loop

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: different edit from a: compute the sanitised alias once per user and reuse in the read loop

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: `if remaining:` after `if not remaining: return` always holds; delete the test. Expected gain nil

what_it_does: inserts a member entry into the sorted Emeritus section of a README string, or creates the section

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: one pass over `lines` records the matching lines and first/last index, instead of two full regex passes over the same lines

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: module-level compiled pattern replaces the three string-pattern re.match calls per line; distinct edit from a

what_it_does: extracts member dicts from a README section by running a multiline regex

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the append loop becomes a list comprehension

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: hoist the constant pattern into a module-level compiled object; saves the re cache lookup per call

what_it_does: finds a section's start/end offsets via two compiled patterns

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `Looks like it, but is not`: the start pattern embeds the section name and the end pattern the header level, so there is no single artefact to hoist, and re's own cache already serves repeated identical patterns

what_it_does: removes a user's list line from a README section

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the README string changes after each successful removal and the only callers are in create_emeritus_prs, so the section offsets cannot be reused between calls; no single-call repair exists

what_it_does: formats the PR body markdown with one line per changed member

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: body is a plain unaliased local grown by += per member; collecting lines and joining once removes the per-append reallocation risk

what_it_does: formats the issue body markdown with one line per changed member

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: same shape as _build_pr_body: += per member, replaced by one join

what_it_does: for each repo, edits the fetched README per inactive user and opens a PR or issue via the API

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the README string is rewritten after each removal and addition, so cached section offsets would be stale; each re-scan is on changed text. Also network-bound

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: the teams list per user holds a handful of names; list membership there costs nothing worth a repair

what_it_does: validates ids, parent chains, required roles, team membership and collective sponsorship for each workstream

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the teams lookup and three set comprehensions over people_data depend only on people_data; building them once before the loop stops rebuilding them per workstream

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `parent_kind` and its dict lookup are dead; deleting the line removes a get and a get per iteration with a parent

what_it_does: renders a README table of SIGs, one row per workstream

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: extract_row_data builds notes, discussion, repo, roadmap and people strings per SIG that this renderer never reads; a lighter extraction of just schedule, calendar and slack avoids that. Edits extract_row_data's callers only if shared, and render_sig_details uses the full function, so the new helper is added beside it

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: distinct edit from a: build rows in a list and join once instead of += per row

what_it_does: concatenates per-SIG detail blocks under a heading

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: += per SIG replaced by a join over the detail blocks

what_it_does: reconciles existing voter comments with the roll: strips stale handles, deletes empty comments, posts new batches

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: each comment body is regex-scanned for mentions twice (tagged set, then stale scan); a single scan cached per comment serves both

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: a single-pass multi-handle removal would have to reproduce remove_handle_line's `\s*(?:\n|$)` consumption and case-insensitive matching exactly; the rewrite is not a small edit and its equivalence is doubtful

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: remove_handle_line removes every line for a handle, so the number of removals does not tell whether mentions remain; the rescan is needed

what_it_does: deletes every list line for a handle from a comment body

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the pattern embeds the handle, so each call compiles a pattern for a different handle and re's cache already covers repeats; no hoistable artefact

what_it_does: tests whether a comment's first line equals the header

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: splitlines() splits on \r, \x0b, \x0c, \x1c-\x1e, \x85, \u2028 and \u2029; any cheaper first-line extraction changes which bodies match, and comment bodies are short

what_it_does: aggregates job records per (repo, workflow) and renders a Markdown table

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `runs` is a set of run ids that always equals run_totals' key set; len(run_totals) gives n_runs, so the set add per record goes away

what_it_does: fetches runs and jobs per workflow through `gh` and builds per-job records

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: each `gh api` call is a subprocess waiting on the network, run one after another; a thread pool overlaps the waits. Energy impact is uncertain because the process spawns multiply

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: parse_iso(started) is evaluated up to three times per job; bind once

what_it_does: looks up the GitHub login for each devstats user and builds [login, contributions] rows

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: each lookup is a blocking HTTP call plus a 100 ms sleep, serial; overlapping them with a pool shortens the wait but the sleep exists to throttle, so energy effect is uncertain

what_it_does: orders GC members by load descending then name

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: list(load.items()) followed by .sort() builds the list and then sorts it in place; sorted(load.items(), key=...) does the copy once. Same result
